strengths: Owner RLS plus explicit grants and composite child-parent ownership FKs
Run snapshots, profile/claim revisions and input hashes retain document lineage without requiring full normalization

Guest support has hashed private receipts, atomic quotas, expected-version staff updates and a 90-day cleanup function

findings.problem: New run enrollment can reactivate an account during erasure, allowing a private artifact upload after the eraser's prefix scan. Final SQL erasure removes authority but can leave the object retained. This is not an observed public exposure.

evidence.detail: Enrollment reactivates inactive seats; start_run invokes it at lines 47-51.
begin_erase deactivates/cancels existing state; storage insertion only requires active seat plus record at lines 247-256; finish_erase deletes SQL state at 257-269.
Scans prefix first, deletes collected objects, then calls finish_erase; no durable erasing fence or final rescan.

Command: node .tmp/20-role-review/03-database-architect/erase-interleave.mjs. In-memory synthetic PGlite fixture asserts reactivated seat, zero records, zero runs, one storage object and private bucket after interleaving begin/start/upload/finish; exit 0.

findings.recommendation: Add durable erasing state/generation checked by every mutation, enrollment, scheduling, run/OAuth operation and storage insert. Keep fence through storage deletion plus final empty-prefix verification, and persist retry progress.
acceptance_criteria: Two-session begin_erase/start_run/upload interleaving rejects new work and uploads
Interrupted deletion retries reach empty storage prefix, no career/run/packet/connection records and inactive seat
Committed shared budget is unchanged by erasure
Explicit subsequent fresh enrollment is possible only after erasure completion
dependencies: Storage guard and synthetic concurrency regression
findings.cost_effect: Reduces orphan storage and manual deletion support; requires no new service.

findings.problem: Record mutation locks the record before updating runs, while phase commit locks the run before the record. Concurrent correction and commit can deadlock; actual production occurrence is unverified.

evidence.detail: Current write_record locks account record at 169 and updates active runs at 175.
commit_phase locks run, then account record at 139.
A factual edit can overlap worker phase commit. PostgreSQL can abort one transaction, causing a retry/error; no runtime incident claimed.

findings.recommendation: Standardize account/record-first serialization across mutation, start, commit, erase and approval functions; preserve stale-input and lease guards.
acceptance_criteria: Real PostgreSQL two-connection correction/commit stress test records no SQLSTATE 40P01
Concurrent correction still prevents publication of old facts
CAS conflict remains actionable and retry does not duplicate packets or provider cost
findings.cost_effect: Reduces transient support and wasted worker execution; no paid dependency.

findings.problem: Every snapshot fetch loads full bodies for 30 runs and 150 packets. Run snapshots are discarded in the public mapping; packet and usage owner-list indexes are absent. No measured latency failure is asserted.

evidence.detail: select('*') list queries at 46-47; usage owner query at 48; publicRun mapping at 105-107 drops run snapshot.
Run snapshot and data allow 2 MB each; packet body allows 1 MB at 33. Existing run owner-date index at 24 does not cover packet listing.
recoverableRuns limits twenty before applying lease expiry in application memory.

findings.recommendation: Fetch summary projections and deterministic cursor pages, fetch full selected packet on demand, add measured owner/date and owner/run access indexes, and filter recoverable lease expiry before LIMIT.
acceptance_criteria: Measure representative ten-user response bytes before/after
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) confirms intended owner-list and recovery paths
Cursor pages have no duplicates/omissions across identical timestamps
Selected packet text, evidence and approval hashes remain identical
findings.cost_effect: Lowers database transfer, JSON decoding and refresh work; no distributed infrastructure required.

findings.problem: Signed-in support uses separate count and insert operations without an idempotency request ID; concurrent submissions can exceed quota and ambiguous retries duplicate requests.

evidence.detail: Counts prior requests at 81, checks limit at 82, then independently inserts at 83.
Support table has generated ID but no owner/request uniqueness.
Guest equivalent already serializes quota and replays same request at lines 31-42.

findings.recommendation: Use one service-only signed-in intake RPC with owner/request uniqueness, payload conflict checks and atomic daily quota, following the guest receipt implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Ten parallel new requests for one account admit five
Other owners and browser roles cannot inspect privileged support intake
dependencies: Atomic intake migration and fixture tests
findings.cost_effect: Reduces duplicate staff work and unbounded retry writes.
